generated.title: Will California Fall Into the Ocean? Myth vs Fact #shorts
generated.description:
Myth: California will fall into the ocean. Fact: there's nowhere for it to fall.

California sits where the Pacific and North American plates meet, along the San Andreas Fault System. The plates slide past each other, sideways, with the Pacific Plate moving northwest relative to the North American Plate at about 46 millimeters a year. Southwestern California is moving north, and at that rate USGS says Los Angeles and San Francisco will one day (about 15 million years from now) be next-door neighbors.

The map, fault trace, arrows and the accelerated Los Angeles move in this video are schematic illustrations, not data or footage.

Part of the Earthquake Science Explained series. Subscribe to Next Huge Quake for more earthquake science.
